admission.justification: A leaf's latest row about a subject governs, so without this rule a row written after a closeout could replace the judgment of a changed record with a no_impact row, and the change would land with no effect and no reason recorded.

applicability: The history rows of a leaf on converted memory about an invariant or a family whose record the leaf changed and has not landed on its parent line. This also covers an ordinary converted-memory leaf's writer run when its persisted worklist supplies the comparison facts.
conditions: The invariant's revision, or the family's guarantee, in the candidate differs from the parent line's.
At a commit that publishes a leaf, the validator judges the history files no comparison base holds closed; the gate judges the current governing row against its comparison facts.
The writer's additional same-run check consumes the persisted leaf worklist and applies the shared changed-record or changed-family predicate to every matching item.
exclusions: A change that has landed on the leaf's parent line: a leaf reopened after its integration may answer the record with a row of any disposition.
A master's or checkpoint's landing, which is not refused for one of its leaves' rows.
A changed row replaced by hand inside one attempt, which the validator's rule cannot see; the gate's rule does.
The retired database-era realization site; the obligation is recorded on converted memory only.
Wave and crossing owners have no leaf worklist; the writer's persisted-leaf-worklist check does not apply to those owners.
statement: While a leaf's candidate holds another revision of an invariant, or another guarantee of a family, than the leaf's parent line, the leaf's governing row about that record -- its latest across its attempt files -- is the changed row of that change, or the row that retires the record. A later no_impact, moved or extended row about such an invariant, or a no_impact, assigned or rerouted row about such a family, leaves the item open at the gate and is refused by the validator at a commit that publishes the leaf. The writer accepts a changed row at an unchanged revision only as a restatement of the leaf's own changed row of that revision in an earlier attempt. The writer also enforces this governing-row rule before writing: for an ordinary leaf with a persisted worklist, every matching touched_invariant or stale_invariant item with a different recorded base revision, and every reached_family item flagged guarantee-changed, is checked by the same rule in the same run. A preceding item with no base revision does not waive a later matching changed-record item.
